rounds.text: Anka India Ltd is severely mispriced after an aggressive sell-off that leaves the stock sitting just 5% of the way up its 52-week range near a low of 19 against a 71 high [E4]. Despite this depressed valuation, the underlying business demonstrates explosive multi-year growth potential, evidenced by a massive 132% compounded sales growth rate over three years [E13] alongside a 23% compounded profit growth rate over the same period [E15]. Recent operational momentum confirms this structural capability, with profit growth exceeding one-year price growth by 47% as the company begins to outperform expectations [E45], supported directly by positive screen signals for year-over-year profit growth exceeding 20% [E53] and quarter-over-quarter sales increases [E55]. Furthermore, the company operates within a strong macroeconomic tailwind, benefiting from a robust sector median profit growth of 19.2% [E63] and sector median sales growth of 16.1% [E64]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a 19% contraction in compounded sales [E14], an 8% drop in compounded profits [E16], a negative return on assets of -1.27% [E7], and a zero dividend yield [E3].
